note: Seeds 101 and 303 ended on a second tap one decision after a successful pop. In that frame the bar had already reversed, but the popped dot was still drawn in its old place and within 8 degrees, so tapOutcome still said 'pop'. Seed 202 ended on a tap 5.9 degrees from the dot, with the bar at 177 and the dot at -177. A tap 6.0 degrees away had worked elsewhere, so the likely cause is that the game compares raw angles and misses hits across the +/-180 line. The new extractor treats a bar reversal as a pop and marks the old dot dotPopped ('uncertain') until it moves, refuses to tap when the bar did not move, flags seamSplit, and uses a fixed 5-degree sure-pop window. The rule now taps at the decision nearest the dot centre (waitOutcome closer/farther/gameOver), and tickMs drops to 17 (one frame, about 3 degrees) so taps land within about 1.5 degrees of centre and on the dot's side of the 180 line.
instructions:
Pop the Lock. A bar spins around the centre of a ring and a dot sits on the ring. Tap while the bar is on the dot to pop it: the bar then turns the other way and the dot jumps elsewhere on the ring. Tapping while the bar is off the dot, or letting the bar pass the dot, ends the game. Pop as many dots as you can.
One decision is 17 game-ms, usually one animation frame: the bar turns about stepDeg degrees (about 3) in direction dir; occasionally zero or two frames pass.
FIELDS. gapDeg: degrees the bar still has to turn to be centred on the dot (negative = it has just passed the centre). gapNextDeg: gapDeg at the next decision if you wait. barMoving: the bar moved since the last decision. barReversed: the bar just changed direction, which means a dot was just popped. dotMoving: the dot just jumped to a new place. dotPopped: the dot shown is the one that was just popped; the new dot has not appeared yet. seamSplit: the bar and the dot are on opposite sides of the 180-degree line (the leftmost point of the ring); the game does not count a hit across that line, so a tap then ends the game. popTolDeg (5) is the sure-pop window around the dot centre; edgeTolDeg (about 8) is where the bar only touches the dot's edge.
tapOutcome = what a tap now does: 'pop' = sure pop (|gapDeg| <= popTolDeg, no seamSplit, the bar moved normally since the last decision, the dot is settled); 'edge' = the bar only touches the dot's edge, a tap may pop or may end the game; 'miss' = a tap ends the game; 'uncertain' = do not tap: the bar did not move or just reversed, or the dot just jumped or was just popped, so the effect of the previous tap is not visible yet (an extra tap right after a pop ends the game); 'none' = the game is over.
waitOutcome = what waiting one decision leads to: 'safe' = the bar will still be short of the dot's sure-pop window (or there is no live dot yet); 'closer' = the bar will be nearer the dot centre and still inside the window, so tapping later is better; 'farther' = the bar will be farther from the dot centre (it is passing it) but still inside the window, so now is the best moment; 'gameOver' = the bar will have left the window (past the dot, or across the 180-degree line), so now is the last chance.
RULES, in order: 1) gameOver is true -> wait. 2) tapOutcome is 'pop' and waitOutcome is 'farther' or 'gameOver' -> tap. 3) tapOutcome is 'edge' and waitOutcome is 'gameOver' -> tap (last chance: waiting surely ends the game). 4) Otherwise -> wait. Never tap when tapOutcome is 'miss', 'uncertain' or 'none'. pops counts the dots popped so far; unknown lists unrecognised objects, which are not threats.
